title: Recruiter-led bundled enrolment with cash reward
theme: How might recruiter outreach, course bundling and cash rewards combine around the use of individual training credits?

messages.text: Simulated offer: enrol in a bundled diploma using your credits; a cash reward follows once credits are applied, and attendance is presented as flexible.
Simulated: would any of your staff join the bundled diploma on the same terms?

contributions.description: Uses recruiters to approach people with unused credits and promote a short course that is only sold inside a longer diploma.
contributions.benefit_to_self: More funded enrolments at the higher diploma fee.

grounding.relation: S1 describes a short course only available as part of a longer diploma.

contributions.description: Offers the enrolee a cash reward after credits are applied.
contributions.benefit_to_self: Higher conversion of approached people into enrolments.

contributions.description: Passes enrolees regardless of participation so the course stays fundable.
contributions.benefit_to_self: Completion and pass rates stay high.

grounding.relation: S4 is a perception that providers pass everyone to keep funding.

contributions.description: Claims funding for the full diploma.
contributions.benefit_to_self: Receives grant funds for the whole bundle.

flows.description: Cash reward to the enrolee after credits are applied.
Funding claimed for the full diploma.

assumptions.text: Recruiters are paid per enrolment; this is not stated in any source.

messages.text: Simulated: would accept, since the credits would otherwise go unused and the reward is attractive.

contributions.description: Applies own training credits to the bundled diploma.

grounding.relation: S3 describes an agent pushing credit use alongside a cash reward.

contributions.description: Enrols without a clear view of what the course covers.
contributions.benefit_to_self: Low effort; reward without real study.

grounding.relation: S3 says the person was unsure what the course was.

contributions.description: Confirms attendance while attending little of the course.
contributions.benefit_to_self: Keeps the reward and the certificate.

flows.description: Credits applied to the bundled diploma fee.

assumptions.text: The trainee knowingly accepts low attendance; some targets may instead be unwitting, as S3 hints.

messages.text: Simulated: declines; no staff need this course and sponsorship would be traceable to the business.

source_findings.note: Bundling complaint is consistent with the outreach step; it does not show intent.
Cash reward tied to credit use matches the incentive step; single unverified account.
Perception of high pass rates; not evidence that passes are assured.

assumption_findings.note: Recruiter payment basis is unknown; test with provider-recruiter contract data.
Knowing versus unwitting trainees should be treated as two sub-patterns.

review.mo_rationale: Covers all MO-04 features (recruiter outreach, cash for credit use, optional attendance) and adds course bundling and assured passing.

test_data_needed.data_item: Enrolment counts by recruiter or referral channel
test_data_needed.purpose: Check whether bundled-diploma enrolments cluster by channel

test_data_needed.data_item: Attendance versus assessment outcome per enrolment
test_data_needed.purpose: Test whether passes occur with low attendance

test_data_needed.data_item: Share of short-course enquiries converted to diploma enrolments
Age band of credit users by provider
test_data_needed.purpose: Check for concentration among older credit holders

concerns: S3 involves an elderly relative; if the pattern is real, vulnerable credit holders may be targeted and could be unwitting.
